headline: ChatGPT and Codex experiencing elevated error rates, OpenAI confirms
summary: Users are reporting issues with OpenAI's popular AI models, with the company acknowledging elevated error rates on its system status page.
details: OpenAI's system status page has confirmed that users are encountering elevated error rates when attempting to use both ChatGPT and Codex.
The issue appears to be widespread, affecting users who rely on these AI models for various tasks. Specific details regarding the cause or expected resolution time have not yet been provided.

ChatGPT is a powerful language model capable of generating human-like text, while Codex is an AI system that translates natural language into code. Outages or performance degradation can significantly impact workflows for developers and content creators.
This incident highlights the ongoing challenges in maintaining the stability and reliability of large-scale AI services. Further updates are expected from OpenAI as they investigate the root cause.

headline_marked: AMD's X100 APUs [[power physical AI]] with Zen 5, RDNA 3.5
headline: AMD's X100 APUs power physical AI with Zen 5, RDNA 3.5
summary: New processors for robotics boast up to 5.1 GHz boost clock, 128 GB unified memory, and 50 TOPS NPU.
details: AMD has unveiled its new X100 series of processors, designed to bring the power of their Strix Halo APUs to physical AI applications, particularly in robotics. These chips are built for 24/7 operation and feature a 10-year lifecycle for embedded systems.

The X100 lineup includes three models: the X199 with 16 Zen 5 cores and 40 RDNA 3.5 CUs, the X188 with 12 cores and 32 CUs, and the X168 with eight cores and 32 CUs. They offer boost clocks up to 5.1 GHz, 128 GB of unified memory, and an XDNA 2 NPU capable of 50 TOPS.

These processors are designed to reduce latency by integrating CPU, AI accelerator, and memory onto a single chip, directly competing with Intel's Panther Lake SoCs for physical AI. The X100 range is physically larger, packing more silicon for more potent deployments.

AMD claims significant performance advantages over Intel's Core Ultra X7 358H, with benchmarks showing leads of up to 1.5x in integer workloads and 1.7x in graphics performance. However, these comparisons involve projected performance for the Intel chip and a different TDP configuration.

For AI inference, AMD claims a 1.4x improvement in Time to First Token and 3.5x faster tokens per second in Llama-bench when running at a 45W TDP. These figures were based on tests using a Ryzen AI Max 395+ configured to match X199 specs, with the Intel chip's performance extrapolated.

Beyond the chips, AMD is offering X100 models via Kria System on Modules (SOMs) and a comprehensive robotics developer platform. This platform, available in early access, includes specialized connectivity for cameras and industrial networking, aiming to be a turnkey solution for robotics development.
AMD is also actively encouraging developers to move from Nvidia's CUDA platform to its own HIP C++ portable code using its HIPIFY tool, which can convert CUDA code to HIP.
